newsitem.title: USA: ORLANDO, FLA., AIRPORT EXPANSION WINS CARRIER OKAY.
newsitem.headline: ORLANDO, FLA., AIRPORT EXPANSION WINS CARRIER OKAY.

text.p: Major carriers at Florida's Orlando International Airport have approved a $965 million expansion plan that relies heavily on bond financing, the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority said Wednesday.
The project will add a fourth satellite terminal to the airport's north terminal complex, construct a new air traffic control tower and begin work on a new south terminal complex.
The plan was approved by the airport's 11 signatory airlines, the major carriers with long-term leases who have oversight on debt financing that would affect their rents.

They are AirTran Airways, AMR Corp unit American Airlines, American Trans Air, Comair, Continental Airlines Inc, Delta Air Lines, Northwest Airlines Corp, Southwest Airlines, TWA, United and US Airways.

"The approval by the airlines is a joint effort because the projects are demand-based with appropriate safeguards to ensure that facilities will be provided in a phased way as passenger demands continue to develop," said Bob Hattaway, chairman of the aviation authority.

Passenger traffic at the fast-growing airport reached a record 25 million last year. The airport's 13.9 percent growth rate for 1996 was the highest of any of the top 30 airports in the world for the period.
The expansion program will add a fourth satellite terminal with at least 16 gates in the north terminal complex, with a people mover connecting it to the main terminal.

It includes improvements to baggage handling and elevator systems, construction of a new air traffic control tower and north crossfield taxiway, and design and partial construction of the first phase of the new south terminal, including at least 16 gates.
The projects are scheduled to begin in the fall with completion expected early in the next century.

The financing plan for the expansion calls for $432 million of revenue bonds backed by landing fees and airport rents and another $331 million backed by passenger facility charges. Most of the remaining money would come from federal grants.

The expansion plan approved by the carriers on Wednesday follows the approval of a $240 million near-term construction that will double the number of public parking spaces, improve motor vehicle traffic circulation and provide group check-in facilities.
